questions.question: Exam Pass or Fail: Accept a student's marks. A student passes if marks are 35 or above. Display pass or fail. (if / if-else)
Scholarship Eligibility: Accept a student's marks. The student is eligible for a scholarship if marks are 90 or above.
Library Book Access: Check whether a student can borrow a book based on whether they have a valid library card.
Attendance Eligibility: Accept attendance percentage. A student is eligible for the examination if attendance is at least 75%.
Age-Based Admission: Accept a child's age. The child is eligible for admission if they are at least 5 years old.
ATM Withdrawal: Accept account balance and withdrawal amount. Allow the withdrawal only if the balance is sufficient.
Minimum Bank Balance: Accept an account balance. Mark the account as low balance if it is below ₹1,000.
Loan Eligibility: Accept monthly salary. The customer is eligible for a basic personal loan if the salary is ₹25,000 or above.
UPI PIN Verification: Accept a PIN. Allow the payment only if the PIN matches the registered PIN.
Fixed Deposit Eligibility: Accept a customer's age. The customer qualifies for the senior citizen scheme if they are 60 or above.
Free Delivery Eligibility: Accept an order amount. The customer gets free delivery if the order is worth ₹500 or more.
Product Stock Availability: Accept available stock. The product can be ordered only if at least one unit is available.
Discount Eligibility: Accept a purchase amount. The customer gets a 10% discount if the purchase is ₹2,000 or above.
Coupon Validation: Accept a coupon code. The coupon is valid only if it is SAVE100.
Return Request: Accept the number of days since delivery. The product is eligible for return only within 7 days.
Employee Login: Accept a password. The employee can log in only if the password is correct.
Bonus Eligibility: Accept an employee's years of experience. The employee qualifies for the bonus if they have at least 2 years of service.
Overtime Payment: Accept working hours in a day. The employee is eligible for overtime if they worked more than 8 hours.
Leave Approval: Accept available leave days. The employee can apply for leave only if at least one leave day remains.
Work-from-Home Eligibility: Accept the manager's approval status. The employee can work from home only if the request is approved.
Blood Donation Eligibility: Accept a person's age. The person is eligible to donate blood if they are at least 18.
Hospital Appointment: Accept slot availability. The appointment can be confirmed only if a doctor's slot is available.
Gym Membership Discount: Accept the membership type. The customer qualifies for the discount if they bought an annual membership.
BMI Health Check: Accept a BMI value. The person is classified as overweight if BMI is 25 or above.
Medicine Availability: Check whether the requested medicine is in stock. It can be provided only if it is available.
Driving License Eligibility: Accept a person's age. The person may apply for a driving license if they are 18 or above.
Train Ticket Confirmation: Accept available seats. A ticket can be booked only if at least one seat is available.
Vehicle Speed Monitoring: Accept vehicle speed. The vehicle is overspeeding if its speed exceeds 80 km/h.
Fuel Availability: Accept available fuel and required fuel. The journey is possible only if available fuel is at least the required amount.
Parking Fee Eligibility: Accept a shopping amount. The customer gets free parking if they spend ₹1,000 or more.
File Upload Validation: Accept a file size in MB. The file can be uploaded only if it is 5 MB or less.
Internet Data Availability: Accept available data in MB. The update can be downloaded only if at least 100 MB is available.
Website Access Control: Accept a user's role. Dashboard access is allowed only if the role is admin.
Password Strength Check: Accept a password. It is valid only if it has at least 8 characters.
Software Update Notification: Accept the installed version and the latest version. An update is required if the installed version is lower.
Restaurant Table Booking: Accept the number of available tables. A reservation can be made only if at least one table is available.
Food Order Minimum Amount: Accept the order amount. The order can be placed only if it is ₹100 or above.
Kitchen Order Processing: Accept payment status. The kitchen should start preparing the order only after payment is confirmed.
Food Expiry Check: Accept the expiry status of a product. The product cannot be sold if it has expired.
Customer Feedback Reward: Accept feedback submission status. The customer receives a free dessert if they submitted feedback.
Movie Ticket Eligibility: Accept a person's age. They can watch a 12+ movie only if they are 12 or above.
Gaming Level Unlock: Accept a player's score. The next level unlocks only if the score is at least 100.
Tournament Registration: Accept payment status. The player can participate only if the registration fee is paid.
Swimming Pool Entry: Accept membership status. The person can enter the pool only if the membership is active.
Online Video Access: Accept subscription status. Premium video access is allowed only if the premium subscription is active.
Electricity Bill Alert: Accept monthly consumption in units. A high-usage alert is generated if consumption exceeds 300 units.
Water Tank Monitoring: Accept the water level percentage. A notification is sent if the level is 90% or above.
Parcel Delivery Status: Accept the delivery confirmation status. The parcel is marked delivered only if the agent confirmed delivery.
Weather Alert System: Accept the current temperature. A heat alert is generated if the temperature is 40°C or above.
Smart Door Lock: Accept a security code. The door unlocks only if the code matches the registered code.
Warehouse Storage Classification: Accept storage percentage. Low (below 30%), Medium (30–60%), High (61–85%), Critical (above 85%). Display the category using if-elif-else.
Package Weight Classification: Accept package weight in kg. Light (below 1), Medium (1–5), Heavy (6–15), Extra Heavy (above 15).
Inventory Reorder Status: Accept available quantity. Out of Stock (0), Low Stock (1–10), Moderate Stock (11–50), Sufficient Stock (above 50).
Warehouse Temperature Monitoring: Accept temperature in °C. Freezing (below 0), Cold (0–5), Normal (6–15), Warm (above 15).
Product Shelf-Life Classification: Accept remaining shelf-life in days. Critical (0–5), Short (6–15), Moderate (16–30), Long (above 30).
Machine Performance Classification: Accept machine efficiency %. Poor (below 50), Average (50–70), Good (71–90), Excellent (above 90).
Production Target Evaluation: Accept daily production units. Below Target (below 500), Target Achieved (500–700), Above Target (701–1,000), Outstanding (above 1,000).
Raw Material Quality: Accept inspection score. Rejected (below 40), Acceptable (40–60), Good (61–80), Excellent (above 80).
Machine Maintenance Priority: Accept operating hours. Low (below 100), Medium (100–500), High (501–1,000), Critical (above 1,000).
Defective Product Percentage: Accept defect rate %. Excellent (below 1), Acceptable (1–3), Warning (above 3–5), Critical (above 5).
Soil Moisture Classification: Accept soil moisture %. Dry (below 20), Moderate (20–40), Moist (41–70), Wet (above 70).
Crop Growth Stage: Accept crop age in days. Seedling (0–15), Vegetative (16–40), Flowering (41–60), Maturity (above 60).
Rainfall Classification: Accept rainfall in mm. Light (below 10), Moderate (10–50), Heavy (51–100), Very Heavy (above 100).
Fertilizer Requirement: Accept a soil nutrient level. Deficient (below 20), Low (20–40), Balanced (41–70), Rich (above 70).
Farm Equipment Fuel Consumption: Accept tractor fuel use in litres per hour. Low (below 2), Normal (2–5), High (6–8), Excessive (above 8).
Property Size Classification: Accept property size in sq. ft. Small (below 500), Medium (500–1,000), Large (1,001–2,000), Luxury (above 2,000).
Building Floor Classification: Accept number of floors. Low-Rise (1–4), Mid-Rise (5–10), High-Rise (11–20), Skyscraper (above 20).
Construction Progress: Accept completion %. Initial (below 25), Developing (25–50), Advanced (51–75), Nearly Complete (above 75).
Property Age Classification: Accept building age in years. New (below 5), Recent (5–15), Old (16–30), Heritage (above 30).
Room Occupancy Classification: Accept occupancy %. Low (below 30), Moderate (30–60), High (61–85), Full (above 85).
Air Quality Classification: Accept AQI. Good (0–50), Moderate (51–100), Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups (101–150), Unhealthy (151–200), Very Unhealthy (above 200).
Solar Panel Energy Generation: Accept daily generated energy in kWh. Low (below 100), Moderate (100–300), High (301–500), Excellent (above 500).
Noise Pollution Classification: Accept noise level in dB. Quiet (below 40), Moderate (40–60), Loud (61–80), Very Loud (above 80).
Battery Charging Classification: Accept charging rate in kW. Slow (below 2), Normal (2–5), Fast (6–10), Ultra Fast (above 10).
Daily Power Consumption: Accept daily power usage in units. Low (below 50), Moderate (50–150), High (151–300), Excessive (above 300).
Network Latency Classification: Accept latency in ms. Excellent (below 20), Good (20–50), Average (51–100), Poor (above 100).
Server CPU Usage: Accept CPU usage %. Idle (below 20), Normal (20–60), Busy (61–85), Critical (above 85).
Database Response Time: Accept response time in ms. Excellent (below 100), Good (100–300), Average (301–700), Slow (above 700).
Network Packet Loss: Accept packet loss %. Excellent (0), Good (above 0–1), Moderate (above 1–3), Poor (above 3).
Server Memory Usage: Accept memory usage %. Low (below 30), Normal (30–60), High (61–80), Critical (above 80).
Typing Speed Evaluation: Accept typing speed in WPM. Beginner (below 20), Intermediate (20–40), Advanced (41–70), Expert (above 70).
Coding Assessment Classification: Accept coding score. Beginner (below 40), Intermediate (40–60), Advanced (61–85), Expert (above 85).
Language Proficiency Classification: Accept proficiency score. A1 (below 20), A2 (20–40), B1 (41–60), B2 (61–80), C1 (above 80).
Project Completion Evaluation: Accept completion %. Not Started (0), Early Progress (1–25), Halfway (26–50), Advanced (51–75), Completed (above 75).
Training Course Progress: Accept course progress %. Just Started (below 10), In Progress (10–50), Almost Finished (51–90), Completed (above 90).
Tyre Pressure Classification: Accept pressure in PSI. Low (below 25), Normal (25–35), High (36–40), Very High (above 40).
Engine Temperature Classification: Accept temperature in °C. Cold (below 60), Normal (60–100), Hot (101–120), Critical (above 120).
Vehicle Mileage Classification: Accept mileage in km/l. Poor (below 10), Average (10–15), Good (16–20), Excellent (above 20).
Tyre Wear Classification: Accept tread depth in mm. Critical (below 2), Low (2–3), Good (above 3–6), Excellent (above 6).
Vehicle Pollution Classification: Accept emission value. Low (below 50), Moderate (50–100), High (101–200), Excessive (above 200).
Monthly Sales Performance: Accept monthly sales in ₹. Poor (below 50,000), Average (50,000–1 lakh), Good (above 1 lakh–2 lakh), Excellent (above 2 lakh).
Customer Purchase Frequency: Accept purchases per month. Rare (0–1), Occasional (2–4), Regular (5–10), Frequent (above 10).
Website Traffic Classification: Accept daily visitors. Low (below 1,000), Moderate (1,000–5,000), High (5,001–10,000), Viral (above 10,000).
Business Profit Classification: Accept monthly profit in ₹. Loss (below 0), Low Profit (0–10,000), Moderate Profit (10,001–50,000), High Profit (above 50,000).
Customer Support Response Time: Accept response time in minutes. Excellent (below 5), Good (5–15), Average (16–30), Delayed (above 30).
Earthquake Intensity Classification: Accept magnitude. Minor (below 3), Light (3–4.9), Moderate (5–5.9), Strong (6–6.9), Major (7 or above).
Distance Measurement Classification: Accept distance in km. Very Short (below 1), Short (1–5), Medium (6–20), Long (above 20).
Chemical Solution pH Classification: Accept pH value. Acidic (below 7), Neutral (7), Alkaline (above 7).
Sound Frequency Classification: Accept frequency in Hz. Low (below 250), Medium (250–2,000), High (2,001–8,000), Very High (above 8,000).
Scientific Sample Temperature Classification: Accept temperature in °C. Below Freezing (below 0), Freezing Point (0), Cool (1–15), Room Temperature (16–30), Hot (above 30).

Employee Details: An HR application needs to display an employee's name, department, and salary. Define employee_details(name, department, salary) that accepts three positional arguments and displays the employee details.

Calculate Rectangle Area: A construction application needs to calculate the area of a rectangular room using its length and width. Define calculate_area(length, width) that accepts two positional arguments and returns the area.

Student Total Marks: A school wants to calculate a student's total marks in three subjects. Define total_marks(subject1, subject2, subject3) that accepts three positional arguments and returns their total.
Product Information: An online store needs to display product information such as product name, price, and brand. Define product_details(name, price, brand) and call it using keyword arguments.
Movie Information: A movie application needs to display movie name, director, and release year. Define movie_details(name, director, year) and call it using keyword arguments in a different order.
Customer Address: A delivery application needs to store a customer's name, city, and postal code. Define customer_address(name, city, pincode) and call it using keyword arguments.

Mobile Recharge: A mobile application processes recharges using a mobile number, recharge amount, and validity period. Define mobile_recharge(number, amount, validity) and call it by passing the mobile number as a positional argument and the remaining arguments as keyword arguments.

Book Registration: A library maintains book records using book title, author, and publication year. Define book_details(title, author, year) and call it using a combination of positional and keyword arguments.

Flight Booking: An airline application needs passenger name, destination, and ticket class to create a booking summary. Define flight_booking(name, destination, ticket_class) and call it using a positional argument for the passenger name and keyword arguments for the remaining details.

Temperature Conversion: A weather application converts temperature from Celsius to Fahrenheit. Define convert_temperature(celsius, /) that accepts only a positional argument and returns the Fahrenheit temperature. (Hint: use / in the function definition.)

Calculate Square: A mathematical application needs to calculate the square of a given number. Define calculate_square(number, /) that accepts only a positional argument and returns its square. (Hint: use / in the function definition.)

Calculate Discount: A shopping application calculates a discount amount based on the original price and discount percentage. Define calculate_discount(price, percentage, /) that accepts two positional-only arguments and returns the discount amount. (Hint: use / in the function definition.)

Email Notification: An application sends email notifications using the recipient's email address and message. Define send_email(*, email, message) that accepts only keyword arguments and displays the email details. (Hint: use * before keyword-only parameters.)

Hotel Booking Details: A hotel booking system needs the number of guests and number of nights to calculate the total stay duration. Define hotel_booking(*, guests, nights) that accepts keyword-only arguments and displays the booking details. (Hint: use * before keyword-only parameters.)

Product Price Calculation: An online store calculates the final product price using its base price and tax percentage. Define final_price(*, price, tax) that accepts keyword-only arguments and returns the price after adding tax. (Hint: use * before keyword-only parameters.)

Employee Salary Calculation: A company calculates an employee's final salary using basic salary and bonus percentage. Define salary_calculation(basic_salary, /, *, bonus) where basic_salary is positional-only and bonus is keyword-only. Return the final salary. (Hint: use / and * together.)

Distance Conversion: A travel application converts kilometres into miles using a conversion factor. Define convert_distance(kilometers, /, *, conversion_factor) where kilometers must be positional-only and conversion_factor must be keyword-only. (Hint: use / and * together.)

Student Result Generation: An examination system calculates a student's result using total marks and maximum marks. Define student_result(total_marks, /, *, maximum_marks) where total_marks is positional-only and maximum_marks is keyword-only. Calculate and return the percentage. (Hint: use / and * together.)

Shopping Cart Total: An online shopping application allows customers to purchase any number of products and needs to calculate the total price. Define cart_total(*prices) that accepts multiple product prices and returns their total.

Calculate Average Marks: A teacher wants to calculate the average marks of a student across multiple subjects, where the number of subjects may vary. Define calculate_average(*marks) that accepts multiple marks and returns their average.

Restaurant Bill Calculation: A restaurant customer orders multiple food items, and the billing system needs to calculate the total bill. Define restaurant_bill(*items) that accepts multiple item prices and returns the total bill.

Find Maximum Number: A mathematical application receives multiple numbers from a user and needs to identify the largest number. Define find_maximum(*numbers) that accepts any number of positional arguments and returns the largest number.

User Profile Management: A social media application stores different user details such as name, age, city, email, and profession, and different users may have different profile information. Define user_profile(**details) that accepts any number of keyword arguments and displays all the user information.

Product Registration: An inventory application stores product details such as name, price, brand, category, and quantity, and additional details may also be provided. Define register_product(**product_info) that accepts multiple keyword arguments and displays all product information.

Employee Record Management: An HR system stores employee information such as employee ID, name, department, salary, and experience, and the number of details may vary. Define employee_record(**details) that accepts variable-length keyword arguments and displays the employee record.

Greeting Application: A mobile application greets users. If the user does not provide a name, display a default greeting using the name Guest. Define greet_user(name='Guest') that displays a greeting. Call it once without an argument and once with a name. (Hint: assign default values in the function definition.)

Ticket Booking: A cinema application sells movie tickets. The default ticket price is ₹150, but users may choose a different price. Define book_ticket(price=150) that displays the ticket price. Call it with and without an argument. (Hint: assign default values in the function definition.)

Shipping Cost Calculation: An online store charges ₹50 as the default shipping fee, and some special delivery services may have a different charge. Define shipping_cost(amount, delivery_charge=50) that adds the delivery charge to the order amount and returns the total. (Hint: assign default values in the function definition.)

Employee Information: A company stores employee information. If the department is not provided, assign the default department General. Define employee_info(name, department='General') that displays employee details. Call it with and without the department argument. (Hint: assign default values in the function definition.)

Mobile Data Recharge: A telecom application offers a default data recharge of 1 GB, and customers can select a different amount when needed. Define data_recharge(data=1) that displays the selected data amount. Call it with and without an argument. (Hint: assign default values in the function definition.)

Minimum Balance: Create a decorator that checks whether a bank account has a minimum balance of ₹1,000 before allowing a transaction function to execute.
Role-Based Access: Create a decorator that allows only users with the 'admin' role to execute a delete-record function.

Write a generator function that yields only the float values from a given list.
Write a generator function that yields prime numbers from 1 to 10.
Write a generator function that yields the square of each number from 1 to n.
Write a generator function that counts down from n to 1.
Write a generator function that yields one character at a time from a given string.

E-commerce Orders: An e-commerce platform receives thousands of orders every minute. To reduce memory usage, orders should be processed one at a time. Given a list of orders, write a generator that yields one order at a time. Then write code to process each order as it is received.

Student Management System: A school wants to store each student's name, age, roll number, and marks, and calculate the total and average marks. Create a Student class that uses a constructor, keeps name, age, roll_no, and marks as private attributes, stores marks in a list, has instance methods calculate_total() and calculate_average(), calculates the total with a loop, uses >, <, and == to check marks, and then creates two student objects and displays their details.

Bank Account: A bank wants a simple system to manage customer accounts. Customers can deposit and withdraw money, and the balance must not be changed directly from outside the class. Create a BankAccount class with private __account_number, __name, and __balance attributes, a constructor, instance methods deposit() and withdraw(), and a check that rejects withdrawals greater than the balance. Store transactions in a list and display them with a loop.
Bank Account static method: Add a @staticmethod to the BankAccount class that checks whether a deposit amount is valid.
Bank Account class method: Add a @classmethod to the BankAccount class that creates an account from a string such as '101-Ravi-5000'.

Employee Salary System: A company wants to store employee information and calculate salaries. Create an Employee class with private __name, __employee_id, and __salary attributes, a constructor, instance methods display_details() and increase_salary(), a @staticmethod that checks whether a salary is valid, and a @classmethod that creates an employee from a dictionary. Store multiple employees in a dictionary, display all of them with a loop, and find the employee with the highest salary.

Vehicle Rental: A rental company rents cars and bikes. Create a Vehicle class with private __vehicle_number, __model, and __price_per_day attributes, a constructor, and an instance method calculate_rent(days). Create Car and Bike classes that inherit from Vehicle and override calculate_rent() in both. Add a static method that checks whether the number of rental days is valid. Store rented vehicles in a list, display them with a loop, and use > to find vehicles costing more than ₹1,000 per day.

Library Book System: A library wants to maintain books that can be borrowed and returned. Create a Book class with private __title, __author, __price, and __available attributes, a constructor, and instance methods borrow_book(), return_book(), and display_book(). Store books in a list and display the available books with a loop. Add a static method that validates the book price and a class method that creates a book from 'Python Basics-Ravi-500'. Use == to check whether two books have the same title.

Shopping Cart: An online shopping website lets customers add products to a cart. Create a Product class with private __name, __price, and __quantity attributes, and a ShoppingCart class. Use constructors, add products to the cart, remove products from the cart, and store products in a list. Calculate the total price with a loop. Add a static method that validates product price, a class method that creates a product from a dictionary, a @discount decorator that applies a 10% discount, and display the final price.

Mobile Phone: A mobile phone has a brand, model, battery percentage, and installed applications. Create a MobilePhone class with private __brand, __model, __battery, and __apps attributes, and a constructor. Add methods install_app(), remove_app(), and charge_phone(). Store installed apps in a list and display them with a loop. Add a static method that validates battery percentage, a class method that creates a phone from a dictionary, and a decorator that prints 'Phone operation started' before an operation runs.

Simple Product Inventory: A small shop wants to track its products and stock. Create a Product class with private __product_id, __name, __price, and __stock attributes and a constructor. Add add_stock() and sell_product() methods, and prevent selling when stock is insufficient. Store products in a dictionary and product categories in a set. Display products with a loop. Add a static method that validates stock, a class method that creates a product from a dictionary, and a decorator that prints 'Stock updated' after stock changes.
